title: Quantum thermodynamics near the border of a one-dimensional Bose gas
abstract: We consider an ultracold Bose gas in a half-open potential well, otherwise confined to a quasi-one-dimensional geometry. The Bogoliubov equations for its elementary excitations are solved in the continuous spectrum to explore the particle and energy content near the edge of the gas, beyond the often applied local density approximation. In particular, gradients in the condensate density enhance density-dominated excitations in the border region. We discuss excess (missing) particles and their energy by comparing to suitable reference solutions for quasi-homogeneous systems. The density profile near the edge shows no Friedel oscillations, but a dipolar feature from the spill-out of thermally excited particles. The calculations are performed in the grand-canonical ensemble and in the thermodynamic limit.
summary: This paper theoretically examines the quantum thermodynamics of a quasi-1D Bose gas near its physical boundary. It moves beyond simple local approximations by calculating fluctuation corrections to the density and energy. The key finding is the presence of a dipolar density feature at the edge, providing deeper insight into condensate behavior in confined ultracold atomic systems.
main_problem: The study investigates quantum thermodynamic properties, specifically particle and energy content, near the boundary of a quasi-one-dimensional Bose gas, moving beyond the limitations of the local density approximation.
main_result: The density profile near the edge exhibits a characteristic dipolar feature, which is distinct from Friedel oscillations seen in fermionic systems, and the analysis quantifies quantum fluctuation corrections to the density.
method: The research employs Bogoliubov theory within the grand-canonical ensemble, solving excitations using Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations and analyzing energy density corrections up to the second and third order in fluctuations.
model_or_system: The system is an ultracold Bose gas confined in a half-open potential well, modeled using the Gross-Pitaevskii equation for the condensate and Bogoliubov excitations for fluctuations.
key_observables: Density profile, excess/missing particles, surface tension, local compressibility, and the temperature dependence of fluctuation-induced particle density.
important_parameters: The analysis considers various potentials (hard wall, exponential, linear) and operates in the grand-canonical ensemble and thermodynamic limit.
main_assumptions: The calculations avoid the local density approximation, and the analysis relies on expansions in fluctuations, noting that certain corrections vanish in the strict thermodynamic limit.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the condensate edge behavior for various potentials, compare numerical vs. homogeneous particle numbers, and show the temperature dependence of fluctuation corrections for hard vs. exponential potentials.
paper_structure: The paper builds from solving the Bogoliubov equations in the grand-canonical ensemble, deriving energy density corrections, analyzing the boundary effects (dipolar feature), and finally quantifying the temperature dependence of quantum fluctuation corrections.
why_interesting: This work provides detailed, non-LDA descriptions of boundary physics in Bose gases, which is crucial for understanding trapped atom experiments where boundary effects dominate the physics.
